newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia livestock industry needs support - Minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia livestock industry needs support - Minister.

text.p: Russia's ailing livestock industry needs support from the government and abroad to arrest a steady decline in production, Alexander Zaveryukha, Deputy Prime Minister in charge of Russia's harvest, said on Monday.

Zaveryukha said that Russia had agreed with the United States to set up a $100-million fund aimed at stimulating growth in the Russian poultry industry at last week's Gore-Chernomyrdin talks in the U.S.
But he said low domestic livestock prices were discouraging developments in that industry despite stabilising production of grain, of which livestock is a major consumer.
"Overall we are looking at falling production in the livestock industry," he told reporters at a news conference. "So the task of supporting poultry production, is very important for our government."
Zaveryukha said interest among U.S. companies in Russia's agricultural sector was growing, particularly in farm machinery.
Russian delegates at the Gore-Chernomyrdin talks were bombarded with proposals to set up joint farm machinery ventures.
"We have seen a move in the right direction," he told reporters. "There are big U.S. firms who produce farm machinery showing an interest in our market. I don't think these are just words," he said.
In February 1996, a feud between the two countries came to a head when Russia temporarily banned imports of U.S. frozen poultry parts over what it said were problems with salmonella and additives.
The food fight was only resolved after telephone talks between Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and U.S. Vice President Al Gore.
Russia is the largest export market for U.S. poultry, and the business is worth around $500 million a year.
Zaveryukha praised the results of the 1996 grain harvest, which is part of his portfolio.
"It is pleasing that in 1996 we managed to raise grain production (over 1995)," he said.

Russia's official 1996 net grain crop was 69.3 million tonnes compared with 63.4 million tonnes produced in 1995, but despite the recovery, last year's harvest was still one of the lowest crops on record during the last thirty years. --Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +095 941 8520
